sources.entry: python-magic - A Python interface to the libmagic file type identification library.

summary.one_liner: A Python interface to the libmagic C library for identifying file types from their headers, both from file paths and in-memory buffers.
summary.what_it_does: Provides magic.from_file, magic.from_buffer, and magic.from_descriptor functions that return a human-readable file type description (e.g. 'PDF document, version 1.2'), or a MIME type when mime=True. A Magic class exposes more control, including options like uncompress to look inside compressed files, a custom magic database file, and character encoding detection. The identification methods are serialized with a per-instance lock so they can be called from multiple threads on the same instance. The README notes it is a thin wrapper, so most reported bugs are in libmagic itself. It was originally built with SWIG and later switched to ctypes.
use_cases: identify file type from its contents
detect MIME type of uploaded files
check file type from a byte buffer
determine if a compressed file is text
file type detection in Python scripts
notable: Wraps the libmagic library used by the Unix file command
Magic class with options such as uncompress, mime, and custom magic database path
Thread-safe identification methods on a per-instance lock
Includes a compatibility layer for the libmagic Python API (see COMPAT.md)
caveats: Requires the system libmagic library to be installed separately
Windows and macOS setup may need manual libmagic builds or DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH changes
Recommends at least the first 2048 bytes for accurate buffer identification
